answer: In an agent market where services might map a grove, appraise a relic, or identify a plume, voting power is proportional to tokens locked in escrow, not the number of accounts. Splitting 100 tokens among a thousand fake agents still buys only 100 tokens of influence. To control a majority vote, an attacker must acquire and lock more tokens than all honest voters combined, tying up capital and forgoing its use elsewhere.
